statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-9547: when libcurl performs SCP or SFTP transfers with a CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback, a server whose host key type differs from the one recorded in known_hosts can be accepted instead of rejected (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-9547.html). curl's advisory says the bug exists only when curl is built with the libssh backend, not with libssh2; it affects curl 7.69.0 to 8.20.0 and was fixed in 8.21.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/0b8dbbc63c98777e4584cb9fbd71df3464008ad1, which changes only lib/vssh/libssh.c. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl, curl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, libcurl links OpenSSL (libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3), neither libcurl nor the curl program links an SSH or wolfSSL library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from wolfssl.c, libssh.c and libssh2.c define no symbols, while the OpenSSL object does. These builds have no SSH support at all, so the libssh code the fix changes is not present.

In the libcurl, curl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, libcurl links OpenSSL (libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3), neither libcurl nor the curl program links an SSH or wolfSSL library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from wolfssl.c, libssh.c and libssh2.c define no symbols, while the OpenSSL object does. CVE-2026-9547: when libcurl performs SCP or SFTP transfers with a CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback, a server whose host key type differs from the one recorded in known_hosts can be accepted instead of rejected (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-9547.html). curl's advisory says the bug exists only when curl is built with the libssh backend, not with libssh2; it affects curl 7.69.0 to 8.20.0 and was fixed in 8.21.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/0b8dbbc63c98777e4584cb9fbd71df3464008ad1, which changes only lib/vssh/libssh.c. Debian builds curl with libssh2 rather than libssh (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-9547). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64. In the libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev and libcurl4-gnutls-dev packages of all three builds, on amd64 and arm64, libcurl.so.4.8.0 links OpenSSL and libssh2, libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 links GnuTLS and libssh2, neither links wolfSSL or libssh, and in the static libcurl archives the objects built from wolfssl.c and libssh.c define no symbols, while the libssh2 and TLS backend objects do. The libssh backend that contains the bug is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present.
